_meta.author: Mistral Vibe (mistral-vibe)
_meta.purpose: Pilot taxonomy for the humanoid facet. v4 revises only the entity facets (contains_human, contains_robot, contains_android, primary_subject): the v2 depicted-vs-described clause overcorrected -- characters depicted in illustrations, cards, and diagrams must count as visible, and robots require a being-like form (abstract machinery does not count). Representation definitions revert to v2: v3's broadened text_screenshot was a measured negative result (same accuracy on the labeled 50, but five errors became confident and escaped the queue).
design_notes: One revision per re-run (LIBRARY.md Phase 6 discipline): v4 changes only the entity facets, measured against the v2 run on the 50 reviewed records.

The v3 experiment (broadening text_screenshot to game and app screens) is rejected: it converted hedged errors into confident ones -- 22/22 queue-caught errors fell to 16/21. The review's actual semantics are subtler: a screenshot classifies by its content (text screens are text_screenshot; rendered or drawn scenes classify by their rendering).
Depiction includes all media: a human drawn in an illustration, rendered in 3D, or sketched in a diagram is visible and counts. Only bare text mentioning a person does not.
Robots require a being-like form (body, face, or limbs); the review corrected mechanical 'intellect machines' and engines to no.
The 10 contains_human corrections split between over-strict hedges (renders, cartoons) and text-confusions; this revision addresses the former.

GAP (found by the edge-case suite, 2026-09-23, not yet revised): primary_subject has no class for incidental humans -- people visible but not the main subject (e.g., a building with people walking in front). 'none' requires no visible humanoid, so such images fit neither 'human' nor 'none' cleanly; Jev hedges just under the threshold and the queue catches them. Revisit with the library collection, where incidental humans are common.

GAP (found by the edge-case suite, 2026-09-23, not yet revised): representation has no class for an interface screenshot with a depicted subject (e.g., a game inventory screen with a character portrait) -- 'text_screenshot' requires words-not-a-scene, 'other' requires no depicted subject. Jev answers 'other' confidently; the gap is definitional, not a calibration failure. Revisit with the library collection.

contains_human.instructions: Does this image contain a human?

criteria.yes: The image itself shows one or more humans (people, faces, bodies) in any medium: photographed, drawn, illustrated, rendered, or sketched in a diagram. A character depicted in a cartoon, card, or illustration is visible and counts. A person merely mentioned, named, or described in text within the image does not count
criteria.no: The image itself shows no humans: no person, face, or body is visible in any medium (people only mentioned or described in text do not count)

contains_robot.instructions: Does this image contain a robot or mechanical automaton?

criteria.yes: The image itself shows one or more robots: mechanical automatons with a being-like form -- a body, face, or limbs -- whether photographed, illustrated, or rendered. Abstract machinery, engines, or mechanisms without a being-like form do not count; robots merely mentioned or described in text do not count
criteria.no: The image itself shows no robots or mechanical automatons with a being-like form (machinery without a body or face, and robots only mentioned in text, do not count)

contains_android.instructions: Does this image contain an android: an artificial being that passes as human?

criteria.yes: The image itself shows one or more androids: artificial beings manufactured to pass as human, where the image or its context identifies them as artificial. Only what is visible in any medium counts; beings merely described in text do not count
criteria.no: The image itself shows no androids: no artificial beings presented as human-passing (beings only mentioned in text do not count)

primary_subject.instructions: What is the primary humanoid subject of the image?

criteria.human: The main subject the image itself shows, in any medium (photo, illustration, render, diagram), is one or more humans; humans only mentioned or described in text do not count
criteria.robot: The main subject the image itself shows is one or more robots or mechanical automatons with a being-like form; abstract machinery and robots only mentioned in text do not count
criteria.android: The main subject the image itself shows is one or more androids: artificial beings that pass as human
criteria.multiple: The image itself prominently shows more than one distinct kind of humanoid (e.g., a human together with a robot)
criteria.none: The image shows no humanoid subject of any kind, in any medium: no human, robot, or android is visible. Images that are only text, objects, or scenes without humanoids are 'none' -- a humanoid described in text is not depicted

criteria.photograph: A photograph of a real scene: actual people, objects, or places captured by a camera
criteria.illustration: A drawing, cartoon, comic, painting, or digital illustration
criteria.statue_or_render: A statue, figurine, sculpture, model, or 3D render of a subject
criteria.text_screenshot: A screenshot or scan of text: the image shows words or code, not a scene
criteria.other: None of the above: a diagram, chart, map, abstract image, or interface screenshot without a depicted subject
